title: Asian rice domestication begins
note: Archaeological finds from the Lower Yangtze point to rice being domesticated by about 7000 BCE or earlier. Genetic studies disagree on whether Asian rice had one origin or several.

title: Rice reaches the Ganges plain
note: Rice farming is established in northern India. The indica type is thought to have formed here through crossing with local wild rice.

title: Rice reaches mainland Southeast Asia
note: Rice farming spreads south along river valleys into mainland Southeast Asia.

title: Rice reaches Japan
note: Wet-rice farming arrives in northern Kyushu, probably via Korea, around the start of the Yayoi period. Exact dates are debated.

title: African rice domesticated separately
note: A different species (Oryza glaberrima) was domesticated independently in West Africa. The date is approximate.

title: Rice grown around the Mediterranean
note: Rice spreads west through the Middle East and is grown in Iberia by the early Islamic period.

title: Rice farming in the Carolinas
note: Rice becomes a major crop in the Carolina lowcountry. Historians credit the skills of enslaved West Africans who already knew rice farming.

title: Oil palm native to West Africa
note: The oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) is native to the forests of West and Central Africa and has been used for food and oil for thousands of years. The year shown is only a rough guide to early use.

title: Oil palm reaches Brazil
note: Carried across the Atlantic in the 16th century. It became part of local food and culture in Bahia.

title: Four seedlings planted in Java
note: Seedlings planted at Bogor became the parents of the Southeast Asian plantation industry.

title: First commercial plantation in Sumatra
note: Commercial estate planting begins in Sumatra.

title: First commercial estate in Malaya
note: Planting on the Malay Peninsula starts, leading to Malaysia becoming a leading producer.

title: Soybean domesticated in China
note: Written records and archaeology place domestication in China. The exact time and place are debated, and some evidence points to much earlier gradual domestication.

title: Soybean in Korea
note: Archaeological soybeans are found in Korea from the Bronze Age.

title: Soybean in Japan
note: Soybean is farmed in Japan by this time, possibly earlier.

title: Soybean in the Indonesian islands
note: Chinese traders and migrants are thought to have carried soybean into Southeast Asia.

title: Soybean in European gardens
note: Grown as a curiosity in botanical gardens before it became a farm crop.

title: Soybean in North America
note: Samuel Bowen is credited with introducing soybean to the colony of Georgia.

title: Soybean in Brazil
note: First trials in Brazil. Soybean later became a major crop there, and Brazil is now one of the world's largest producers.
